contents.html_ja: 過去1年間、NIST Information Technology Laboratory（ITL）の研究者は、ノイズの非常に多いデバイスで量子コンピューティングを実装する方法を調査しました。この研究は、量子コンピューターが構成要素の不完全さや高い誤り率に耐えられるようになることを意味するため、実用的な量子コンピューティングの開発を加速する可能性があります。ITL の職員は、NIST の物理学者とも協力して、量子鍵生成の達成可能なレートを大幅に高めるシステムを構築しました。そのレートは、従来報告された結果の 100 倍以上高速です。来年、ITL は、耐障害性のある量子コンピューティングの作業を続け、NIST Physics Laboratory と量子構成要素のテストベッドに取り組み、安全なルーティングの問題への量子暗号の応用を調査します。
contents.html: In the past year, NIST Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) researchers investigated methods to implement quantum computing with very noisy devices. This work may speed the development of practical quantum computing because it means that quantum computers will be able to tolerate imperfections and higher error rates in components. ITL staff also worked with NIST physicists to construct a system that represents a major increase in the attainable rate of quantum key generation, over 100 times faster than previously reported results. In the coming year, ITL will continue work on fault-tolerant quantum computing, work with the NIST Physics Laboratory on a test bed for quantum components and investigate applications of quantum cryptography to the problem of secure routing.

contents.html_ja: インターネットが日々の業務と政府の運営に不可欠な部分になるにつれ、インターネットサービスのセキュリティ、安定性および可用性は、国の経済の健全性にとって重要な問題となっています。標準化されたインターネットインフラ保護技術の開発と展開を促進することは、Advanced Network Technologies Division と Computer Security Division が関わる、ネットワーク分野における ITL の主要な重点分野の一つです。私たちは、Domain Name System Security（DNSSEC）プロジェクトを通じて、インターネットの名前解決インフラを保護するための公開仕様の策定を支援しています。もう一つの取り組みは、インターネットのルーティングインフラ、特に Border Gateway Protocol（BGP）において、コンテンツとリソースの両方を保護する標準の策定です。IPSec に関する作業も継続しています。
contents.html: As the Internet becomes an essential part of day-to-day business and government operations, security, stability and availability of Internet services are critical issues to the health of our Nation's economy. Expediting the development and deployment of standardized Internet infrastructure protection technologies has been one of ITL’s major focus areas in networking, involving the Advanced Network Technologies Division and the Computer Security Division.We are helping develop public specifications to secure the Internet naming infrastructure through the Domain Name System Security (DNSSEC) project. Another effort is the development of standards for the protection of both content and resources in the Internet routing infrastructure, in particular, the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). Our work on IPSec has also continued.

contents.html_ja: ドメインネームシステム（DNS）は、http://csrc.nist.gov のようなニーモニック形式のインターネットアドレスを、129.6.13.39. のような対応する数値の IP（インターネットプロトコル）アドレスに変換する方法です。ユーザーとアプリケーションプロセスにとって、この変換は、ローカルホスト、またはインターネット経由のリモートホストが提供するサービスです。DNS サーバーは、自身でアドレスを変換できない場合、インターネット上の他の DNS サーバーと通信することがあります。
contents.html: The Domain Name System (DNS) is the method by which Internet addresses in mnemonic form such as http://csrc.nist.gov are converted into the equivalent numeric IP (Internet Protocol) address such as 129.6.13.39. To the user and application process this transla-tion is a service provided either by the local host or from a remote host via the Internet. The DNS server may communicate with other Internet DNS servers if it cannot translate the address itself.

contents.html_ja: DNS に対する脅威には、いくつかの異なる種類があります。そのほとんどは、より一般的な問題の DNS 関連の事例ですが、一部は DNS プロトコルの特殊性に固有のものです。DNSSEC（DNS Security Extensions の略）は、ドメインネームシステムにセキュリティを追加します。これは DNS の拡張の集合であり、(a) DNS データの出所認証、(b) データの完全性、(c) 認証された不在証明を提供します。DNSSEC は、特定の攻撃からインターネットを保護するために設計されました。
contents.html: There are several distinct classes of threats to the DNS, most of which are DNS-related instances of more general problems, but a few of which are specific to peculiarities of the DNS protocol. DNSSEC (short for DNS Security Extensions) adds security to the Domain Name System. It is a set of extensions to DNS, which provide (a) origin authentication of DNS data, (b) data integrity and (c) authenticated denial of existence. DNSSEC was designed to protect the Internet from certain attacks.

ITL leads the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) DNSSEC editors’ team in the completion and progression of all core DNSSEC specifications. We also work with industry and the Department of Homeland Security to expedite the deployment of these new standards.
contents.html_ja: 私たちは、DNSSEC プロジェクトを通じて、インターネットの名前解決インフラを保護するための公開仕様を策定しています。ITL は、Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）の DNSSEC 仕様編集チームを率いて、DNSSEC のすべてのコア仕様の完成と進展に取り組んでいます。また、これらの新しい標準の展開を促進するため、産業界および国土安全保障省と協力しています。

contents.html: In 2004, NIST achieved several significant mile-stones towards its goal of expediting commercial standards and test and measurement tools for DNSSEC. In addition to leading the IETF DNSSEC editors’ team, we actively participated in the U.S. government DNSSEC Deployment team. We initiated efforts to develop operational plans for the secure operation of .gov and subordinate domains. An initial prototype of the Secure Zone Integrity Tester (SZIT) was completed and put online for diagnosing configuration and operation errors in operational DNSSEC-enabled servers. A NIST Special Publication (SP) 800 Series document, Secure Domain Name System Deployment Guide, was drafted and is being completed by the DNSSEC team. This draft guidance document defines the DNS security problem space, outlines best current practices for securing DNS operations and provides deployment guidance for DNSSEC technologies. Development of an open DNSSEC benchmark framework consisting of measured and cataloged data sets, standard reference models and test scenarios, open source benchmark tools and agreed upon metrics was begun. Development of a DNS zone anonymizer and statistical analysis tools was completed. We collected and statistically analyzed over 2000 DNS zones, developed clustering techniques to facilitate cataloging of zone models and began development of DNS traffic analysis tools.

contents.html_ja: Border Gateway Protocol（BGP）は、自律システム間のルーティングプロトコルです。自律システムとは、共通の管理下にあり、共通のルーティングポリシーを持つネットワークまたはネットワーク群です。BGP は、インターネットのルーティング情報を交換するために使われ、インターネットサービスプロバイダ（ISP）間で使われるプロトコルです。これまで、IT 分野では、潜在的な脅威、リスク、低減技法およびそのコストに関する認識と知識が不足していました。
contents.html: The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is an inter-autonomous system routing protocol. An autonomous system is a network or group of networks under a common administration and with common routing policies. BGP is used to exchange routing information for the Internet and is the protocol used between Internet service providers (ISP). Previously there was a lack of awareness and knowledge in the IT sector of the potential threats, risks, mitigation techniques and their cost.

contents.html: The BGP project was kicked off in February 2004. The project aims to help the industry understand the potential risks to inter-domain routing and the design and implementation trade-offs of the various BGP security mechanisms currently proposed in the IETF community. The project also seeks to expedite convergence towards standardized, implemented and deployed BGP security solutions.

contents.html: In the past year, we made a number of accomplishments. In the attack-modeling framework, we extended the Scalable Simulation Framework (SSF)/Dartmouth BGP discrete event simulation tools with the ability to generate arbitrary focused attacks on BGP infrastructures. We designed a general framework for modeling attacks on BGP protocols. We designed metrics and analysis/visualization tools to characterize the effect of simulated successful BGP attacks, including routing quality metrics, BGP protocol metrics and measured attack properties.

contents.html_ja: Internet Protocol Security（IPSec）は、IP ネットワーク上のプライベートな通信を確保するためのオープン標準の枠組みであり、最も普及したネットワーク層のセキュリティ管理策となっています。IPSec は、機密性、完全性、データ出所認証、パケットのリプレイと通信分析の防止、アクセス保護という、いくつかの種類のデータ保護を提供できます。
contents.html: Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) is a framework of open standards for ensuring private communications over IP networks, which has become the most popular network layer security control. It can provide several types of data protection: confidentiality, integrity, data origin authentication, prevention of packet replay and traffic analysis and access protection.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p39の画像と文字層で照合し、段組みの行断片を読み順の段落・見出し・箇条に組み直した

contents.html_ja: IPSec は、いくつかの構成要素を持つネットワーク層の管理策です。IPSec には、Authentication Header（AH）と Encapsulating Security Payload（ESP）という 2 つのセキュリティプロトコルがあります。AH は、パケットヘッダとデータの完全性保護を提供できます。ESP は、パケットの暗号化と完全性保護を提供できますが、AH のように最も外側の IP ヘッダを保護することはできません。完全性保護の機能は、現在のほとんどの IPSec 実装で使われている ESP の第 2 版に追加されたため、AH の使用は大幅に減少しています。IPSec は通常、IPSec 接続の設定の交渉、鍵の交換、エンドポイント同士の認証、IPSec で保護された接続のセキュリティを定義するセキュリティアソシエーションの確立に、Internet Key Exchange（IKE）プロトコルを使用します。IPSec は、パケットのペイロードを暗号化する前に圧縮するために、IP Payload Compression Protocol（IPComp）を使用することもできます。
contents.html: IPSec is a network-layer control with several components. IPSec has two security protocols – Authentication Header (AH) and Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP). AH can provide integrity protection for packet headers and data. ESP can provide encryption and integrity protection for packets, but cannot protect the outermost IP header, as AH can. The capability for integrity protection was added to the second version of ESP, which is used by most current IPSec implementations; accordingly, the use of AH has significantly declined. IPSec typically uses the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) protocol to nego-tiate IPSec connection settings, exchange keys, authenticate endpoints to each other and establish security associations, which define the security of IPSec-protected connections. IPSec can also use the IP Payload Compression Protocol (IPComp) to compress packet payloads before encrypting them.

contents.html_ja: IPSec にはいくつかの用途があり、最も一般的なのは仮想プライベートネットワーク（VPN）です。これは、既存の物理ネットワークの上に構築された仮想ネットワークで、ネットワーク間で送信されるデータと IP 情報のための安全な通信機構を提供できます。VPN はネットワーク接続のリスクを減らせますが、リスクをなくすことはできません。たとえば、VPN の実装には、攻撃者が悪用できるアルゴリズムやソフトウェアの欠陥、安全でない構成設定や値が含まれている場合があります。
contents.html: IPSec has several uses, with the most common being a virtual private network (VPN). This is a virtual network built on top of existing physical networks that can provide a secure communications mechanism for data and IP information transmitted between networks. Although VPNs can reduce the risks of networking, they cannot eliminate it. For example, a VPN implementation may have flaws in algorithms or software, or insecure configuration settings and values that attackers can exploit.

contents.html_ja: この重要な技術の開発を促進するため、Information Technology Laboratory（ITL）の職員は、IPSec 仕様のリファレンス実装である Cerberus と、IKE の鍵交渉・管理の仕様のリファレンス実装である PlutoPlus を設計し開発しました。インターネット産業のあらゆる分野の多数の組織が、IPSec 技術の高度な課題に関する継続的な研究の基盤として、これらの実装を入手しています。
contents.html: To expedite the development of this crucial technology, Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) staff designed and developed Cerberus, a reference implementation of the IPSec specifications, and PlutoPlus, a reference implementation of the IKE key negotiation and management specifications. Numerous organizations from all segments of the Internet industry have acquired these implementations as a platform for on-going research on advanced issues in IPSec technology.

contents.html_ja: 新たに登場する IPSec 技術の商用実装について、より頻繁で利用しやすい相互運用性試験を求める産業界の声に応えるため、ITL は、Cerberus と PlutoPlus のプロトタイプ実装を土台とする、NIST IPSec WWW-based Interoperability Tester（IPSec-WIT）を開発しました。IPSec-WIT は、試験システムのアーキテクチャと技術に関する実験としても機能します。WWW 技術の斬新な利用により、IPSec-WIT は、試験システムのソフトウェアを配布したり、被試験システムを移設したりすることなく、いつでもどこでも相互運用性試験サービスを提供できます。ITL の職員は、産業界の主要な代表者とも協力して、プロトコル仕様を共同で執筆し、IPSec の設計と標準化のプロセスの進行を妨げていた技術上の行き詰まりを解決しました。
contents.html: To answer an industry call for more frequent and accessible interoperability testing for emerging commercial implementations of IPSec technology, ITL developed the NIST IPSec WWW- based Interoperability Tester (IPSec-WIT), which is built around the Cerberus and PlutoPlus prototype implementations. IPSec-WIT also serves as an experiment in test system architectures and technologies. The novel use of WWW technology allows IPSec-WIT to provide interoperability testing services anytime and anywhere without requiring any distribution of test system software or relocation of the systems under test. ITL staff also collaborated with key industry representatives to co-author protocol specifications and resolve technical impasses that threatened the progress of the IPSec design and standardization process.

contents.html_ja: 昨年、特別刊行物（SP）800-77『Guide to IPSec VPNs』の作業を開始しました。この文書は、VPN アーキテクチャの 3 つの主要なモデル、すなわちゲートウェイ間、ホスト・ゲートウェイ間、ホスト間を記述します。これらのモデルは、それぞれ、インターネット経由で 2 つの保護されたネットワーク（支店と本社など）を接続する、保護されていないネットワーク上のホスト（出張中の従業員など）の通信を保護する、あるいは追加の保護を必要とする 2 台のコンピューター間の直接通信を保護するために使用できます。
contents.html: During the past year, we have begun work on Special Publication (SP) 800-77, Guide to IPSec VPNs. This document will describe the three primary models for VPN architectures – gateway-to-gateway, host-to-gateway and host-to-host. These models can be used, respectively, to connect two secured networks (such as a branch office and headquarters) over the Internet, to protect communications for hosts on unsecured networks (such as traveling employees), or to secure direct communications between two computers that require extra protection.

The five phases of the approach are to identify needs, design the solution, implement and test a prototype, deploy the solution and manage the solution. Special considerations affecting configuration and deployment will be analyzed and three test cases will be presented to illus-trate the process of planning and implementing IPSec VPNs. SP 800-77 will be published in 2005.
contents.html_ja: このガイドは、IPSec の構成要素を記述します。また、IPSec の展開を成功させるのに役立つ、IPSec の計画と実装への段階的アプローチも示します。このアプローチの 5 つのフェーズは、ニーズの特定、ソリューションの設計、プロトタイプの実装と試験、ソリューションの展開、ソリューションの管理です。設定と展開に影響する特別な考慮事項が分析され、IPSec VPN の計画と実装のプロセスを例示する 3 つのテストケースが示されます。SP 800-77 は 2005 年に公表されます。

contents.html_ja: デジタルフォレンジックのコミュニティは、調査で関連する手がかりを明らかにするために使われる可能性のある最新技術に常に遅れずについていくという課題に直面しています。携帯情報端末（PDA）と携帯電話は、今日の社会ではごく一般的で、多くの個人が私的にも業務でも使用しています。携帯デバイスの技術は急速に変化しており、新しい製品と機能が定期的に登場しています。
contents.html: The digital forensic community faces a constant challenge to stay on top of the latest technologies that may be used to reveal relevant clues in an investigation. Personal digital assistants (PDAs) and cellular telephones are commonplace in today’s society, used by many individuals for both personal and professional purposes. Handheld device technologies are changing rapidly with new products and features being introduced regularly.

contents.html_ja: 調査中に PDA や携帯電話に遭遇すると、多くの疑問が生じます。電源の維持について何をすべきか。デバイスをどのように扱うべきか。デバイスに含まれる貴重な、または関連する可能性のあるデータを、どのように調べるべきか。これらの疑問に答える鍵は、PDA のハードウェアとソフトウェアの特性を理解することです。これらのデバイスの構成要素と内部の仕組み（メモリの構成と使用など）を理解することは、デジタルデバイスを扱う際に伴う重大な点を理解するための前提条件です。PDA のメモリ（すなわち RAM）は揮発性であり、パーソナルコンピューターのハードディスクとは異なり、データを保持するために電力が必要です。
contents.html: When a PDA or cellular phone is encountered during an investigation, many questions arise: What should be done about maintaining power? How should the device be handled? How should valuable or potentially relevant data contained on the device be examined? The key to answering these questions is an understanding of the hardware and software characteristics of PDAs. Developing an understanding of the components and inner workings of these devices (such as memory organization and use) is a prerequisite to understanding the criticalities involved when dealing with digital devices. PDA memory (that is, RAM) is volatile and requires power to maintain data unlike a personal computer’s hard disk.

contents.html: CSD has worked this past year to produce SP 800-72, Guidelines on PDA Forensics, which was released as a public draft in August 2004. The intended audience is varied and ranges from response team members handling a computer security incident to organizational security officials investigating an employee-related situation to forensic examiners involved in criminal investi-gations. The practices recommended in this guide are designed to highlight key principles associated with the handling and examination of electronic evidence, in general, and PDAs in particular.

contents.html_ja: 戦略目標 – コンピューターセキュリティ部門（CSD）は、行政府の連邦機関の情報資源の完全性、機密性、真正性を保護するための暗号方式を開発し、改善します。CSD は、政府と産業界が、必要な暗号セキュリティ機能を実装した保証の高い製品を用いて、安全で相互運用可能なアプリケーションを構築できるよう取り組みます。これには、暗号標準と試験方法の継続的な開発、暗号を用いて政府のアプリケーションを保護する方法の開発、鍵管理のガイドラインと方式のさらなる開発、暗号アルゴリズムとともに使用する暗号利用モードの更新と新規作成が含まれます。
contents.html: Strategic Goal – The Computer Security Division (CSD) will develop and improve cryptographic methods for protecting the integrity, confidentiality and authenticity of Federal agency information resources in the Executive Branch. CSD will work to enable government and industry to be able to build secure, interoperable applications with high-assurance products that implement needed cryptographic security functionality. This will include the ongoing development of cryptographic standards and testing methods, developing methods for securing government applications with cryptography, further developing key management guidelines and schemes and the updating and creation of new modes of operation for use with cryptographic algorithms.

contents.html_ja: 暗号に関する私たちの業務は、連邦政府の内外に影響を与えています。強力な暗号は、システムとそれが処理する情報のセキュリティを向上させます。IT ユーザーは、暗号、公開鍵基盤（PKI）、電子認証による安全なアプリケーションが市場でより入手しやすくなることの恩恵も受けています。この分野の業務は、共通鍵暗号技術と公開鍵暗号技術、高度な認証システム、暗号プロトコルとインターフェース、公開鍵証明書の管理、生体認証、スマートトークン、暗号鍵エスクロー、セキュリティアーキテクチャといった話題を扱っています。昨年、国土安全保障に関する大統領令 #12（HSPD-12）が求める作業がこの分野で始まりました。この業務が近い将来に与える影響の例として、連邦職員の識別方法の変更、ユーザーが政府のオンラインサービスを必要とする際の本人認証の方法、米国市民に発行されるパスポートの技術的側面があります。
contents.html: Our work in cryptography is making an impact within and outside the Federal government. Strong cryptography improves the security of systems and the information they process. IT users also enjoy the enhanced availability in the marketplace of secure applications through cryptography, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and e-authentication. Work in this area addresses such topics as secret and public key cryptographic techniques, advanced authentication systems, cryptographic protocols and interfaces, public key certificate management, biometrics, smart tokens, cryptographic key escrowing and security architectures. In the previous year, the work called for in the Homeland Security Presidential Directive #12 (HSPD-12) has begun in this area. A few examples of the impact this work will have in the near future include changes to Federal employee identification methods, how users authenticate their identity when needing government services online and the technical aspects of passports issued to U.S. citizens.

contents.html_ja: この分野の業務は、連邦機関と産業界の両方の多くの主体との連携を伴います。連邦機関には、財務省、Federal PKI Steering Committee と Bridge CA Project に参加している機関、連邦預金保険公社（FDIC）、国家安全保障局（NSA）があります。CSD は最近、金融業界の標準を策定する American National Standards Institute（ANSI）の X9 委員会や、Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）の PKIX ワーキンググループと連携してきました。これらのプロジェクトでの産業界の協力者には、RSA Security Entrust Technologies、International Business Machines（IBM）、Mastercard、Visa、Verizon、VeriSign、Microsoft Corporation があります。
contents.html: This area of work involves collaboration with a number of entities, both from Federal agencies and industry. Some of the Federal agencies include the Department of Treasury, agencies participating in the Federal PKI Steering Committee and Bridge CA Project, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and the National Security Agency (NSA). CSD has worked recently with the American National Standards Institute’s (ANSI’s) X9 Committee that develops standards for the financial industry, as well as with the Internet Engineering Task Force’s (IETF’s) PKIX Working Group. Industry collaborators for these projects have included RSA Security Entrust Technologies, International Business Machines (IBM), Mastercard, Visa, Verizon, VeriSign and Microsoft Corporation.

contents.html_ja: 暗号標準ツールキット（CToolkit）プロジェクトの目的は、米国政府機関などが、データ、通信、業務を保護するための暗号セキュリティの構成要素と機能を選択できるようにすることです。CToolkit は、強力な暗号が世界の政府と産業界で使われること、そして標準アルゴリズムによって安全な相互運用性が達成されることを確保するのに役立ちます。また、CToolkit は、暗号の使用に関するガイダンスと教育も提供します。現在は、暗号化、認証、否認防止、鍵確立、乱数生成のための多種多様な暗号アルゴリズムと技法を含んでいます。CToolkit は標準とガイダンスの集合であり、アルゴリズムの実際のソフトウェア実装は含みません。この作業分野で論じるプロジェクトの多くが組み合わさって、CToolkit を構成しています。
contents.html: The aim of the Cryptographic Standards Toolkit (CToolkit) project is to enable U.S. governmental agencies and others to select cryptographic security components and functionality for protecting their data, communications and operations. The CToolkit helps to ensure that there is worldwide government and industry use of strong cryptography and that secure interoperability is achieved through standard algorithms. The CToolkit also makes guidance and education available in the use of cryptography. It currently includes a wide variety of cryptographic algorithms and techniques for encryption, authentication, non-repu-diation, key establishment and random number generation. The CToolkit is a collection of standards and guidance, and does not include any actual software implementations of the algorithms. Many of the projects discussed in this area of work are combined to form the CToolkit.

Drafts for public review and comment will also be posted for SP 800-38B, Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: The RMAC Authentication Mode (RMAC – Randomized Message Authentication Code), and a revision of SP 800-21, Guideline for Implementing Cryptography.
contents.html_ja: 昨年は、CToolkit に多くの作業が注がれました。NIST 特別刊行物（SP）800-56『Recommendation on Key Establishment Schemes』と、SP 800-57『Recommendation on Key Management』のパート 1 と 2 の最終草案は、2005 年春にパブリックレビュー用に掲載される予定です。SP 800-38B『Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: The RMAC Authentication Mode』（RMAC – Randomized Message Authentication Code）と、SP 800-21『Guideline for Implementing Cryptography』の改訂版についても、パブリックレビューとコメントのための草案が掲載される予定です。

contents.html_ja: 生体認証技術は、身体的または行動的な特徴の認識に基づいて、人物を識別し、またはその身元を検証する自動化された方法で構成されます。消費者は、生体認証に基づく高性能で相互運用可能な（標準に基づく）システムが適時に開発されることを必要としています。標準の適時な策定がなければ、専有システムからオープンシステムの標準に基づくソリューションへの移行は、より困難で費用がかかるものになります。したがって、標準は生体認証プログラムの礎です。国土安全保障と ID 窃盗の防止のために新しい情報技術システムを展開するには、生体認証について、国内および国際的な合意標準の両方が必要になります。NIST は、公式な国内・国際の生体認証標準と関連する適合性評価の策定を加速することにより、オープンシステムの標準に対する政府と市場の要求に応えています。
contents.html: Biometric technologies consist of automated methods of identifying a person or verifying the identity of a person based upon recognition of a physiological or a behavioral characteristic. Consumers need biometric-based high-perform-ance, interoperable (standards-based) systems developed in a timely fashion. In the absence of timely standards developments, migration from proprietary systems to open-systems standard-based solutions will be more difficult and expensive. Therefore, standards are the corner- stone of our biometrics program. Deploying new information technology systems for homeland security and for preventing ID theft will require both national and international consensus standards for biometrics. NIST is responding to government and market requirements for open-system standards by accelerating development of formal national and international biometric standards and associated conformity assessment.

contents.html_ja: これらの標準と関連する適合性評価は、著しく優れたオープンシステムのセキュリティソリューションの展開を支援するため、さらに開発する必要があります。NIST は、そうしたシステムの展開を加速できるよう、これらの標準の策定を後押しする重要なタスクを特定しました。そのため近年、NIST は他の米国政府機関と米国産業界と緊密に連携して、米国にとって関連性の高い公式な国内・国際の生体認証標準の策定を加速するための標準化団体を設立しました。このプログラムは、生体認証標準の標準化と採用を大きく促進します。
contents.html: These standards and associated conformity assessment need further development in order to help deploy significantly better, open-systems security solutions. NIST has identified the critical tasks that will help power the development of these standards so that the deployment of such systems may be accelerated. Consequently, in the past years NIST has worked in close partnership with other U.S. government agencies and U.S. industry to establish standards bodies for accelerating the development of formal national and international biometric standards of high relevance to the U.S. This program is a major catalyst for biometric standardization and adoption of biometric standards.

contents.html_ja: 国内では、生体認証標準プログラムは、InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards（INCITS）のもとに技術委員会 M1 を設立するのを助けました。INCITS M1 の目的は、米国において、公式な国内・国際の汎用生体認証標準を迅速に策定し承認するため、優先度が高く、焦点を絞った包括的なアプローチを確保することです。これらの標準は、国土防衛、ID 窃盗の防止、生体認証に基づくその他の政府・商業用途など、米国のニーズにとって重要と考えられています。私たちは、この標準策定団体に技術面で積極的に貢献しており、その標準策定プロジェクトのいくつかを後援してきました。プログラムの専門家は、NIST の Information Technology Laboratory（ITL）Information Access Division（IAD）の生体認証の専門家と緊密に連携しています。国際的には、International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission Joint Technical Committee 1 Subcommittee 37- Biometrics（ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics）の設立を成功裏に支援しました。INCITS M1 は、JTC1/SC 37 で米国を代表する責任を負う国内技術委員会です。私たちは、この 2 つの標準化団体の議長を務め、その標準プログラムを管理しています。生体認証プロファイルに関する国内標準策定の取り組みでも議長を務めています。U.S. Biometrics Consortium を含む関連コンソーシアムの取り組みにも参加してきました。
contents.html: Nationally, the biometric standards program helped to establish Technical Committee M1 under the InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards (INCITS). The purpose of INCITS M1 is to ensure a high-priority, focused and comprehensive approach in the U.S. for the rapid development and approval of formal national and international generic biometric standards. These standards are considered to be critical for U.S. needs, such as homeland defense, the prevention of identity theft and for other government and commercial applications based on biometric personal authentication. We are active technical contrib-utors to this standards development body and have sponsored several of their standards development projects. The program experts work in close collaboration with NIST’s Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) Information Access Division (IAD) biometric experts. Internationally, we successfully supported the establishment of the International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission Joint Technical Committee 1 Subcommittee 37- Biometrics (ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics). INCITS M1 is the national Technical Committee responsible for representing the U.S. in JTC1/SC 37. We provide the chairperson for these two standards bodies and manage their standards programs. We provide the chair of the national standards development efforts on biometric profiles. We have also participated in related consortia efforts, including the U.S. Biometrics Consortium.

contents.html_ja: 生体認証のインキュベーターと見なされている U.S. Biometric Consortium（BC）は、生体認証に関する米国政府の窓口として機能しています。現在、60 を超える機関、産業界、学界を代表する 900 名を超える会員で構成されています。NIST は、NSA とともに BC の共同議長を務めています。BC は、年次会議、技術ワークショップ、生体認証の技術開発を後援しています。NIST と BC が後援する NIST/BC Biometric Working Group は、ここ数年、政府ユーザーや産業界と協力して、生体認証の仕様を策定してきました。過去には、国内・国際標準としてのさらなる処理のために、(a) Biometric Data Protection and Usage、(b) Biometric Application Programming Interface for Java Card、(c) Common Biometric Exchange File Format の拡張版（CBEFF の初版は NIST 省庁間報告書（NIST IR）6529 として公表されました）の 3 つの仕様を承認し、公式な標準化団体に提供しました。CBEFF の改訂・拡張版は NIST IR 6529-A として公表されました。CBEFF の国際版は、JTC 1/SC 37 内で策定中です。CBEFF は、INCITS M1 と JTC 1/SC 37 内で策定中のすべての国内・国際データ交換標準への適合の要件です。
contents.html: The U.S. Biometric Consortium (BC), which is considered to be a biometrics incubator, serves as a U.S. government focal point for biometrics. It currently consists of over 900 members representing over 60 agencies, industry and academia. NIST co-chairs the BC with NSA. The BC sponsors an annual conference, technical workshops and biometrics technical developments. The NIST/BC Biometric Working Group, sponsored by NIST and the BC has been working in the last few years with government users and industry developing biometric specifications. In the past it approved and provided to formal standards bodies three specifications for further processing as national and international standards, including (a) Biometric Data Protection and Usage; (b) Biometric Application Programming Interface for Java Card, and (c) an augmented version of the Common Biometric Exchange File Format (the initial version of CBEFF was published as NIST Interagency Report (NIST IR) 6529). A revised and augmented version of CBEFF was published as NIST IR 6529-A. An international version of CBEFF is being developed within JTC 1/SC 37. CBEFF is a requirement for conformance for all of the national and international data interchange standards under development within INCITS M1 and JTC 1/SC 37.

contents.html_ja: 暗号利用モード（略してモード）は、機密性や認証などの情報サービスを提供するために共通鍵ブロック暗号アルゴリズムを使用するアルゴリズムです。Advanced Encryption Standard（AES）のような新しいブロック暗号の登場により、長年使われてきた暗号利用モードを更新する必要があり、また新しいモードの開発を検討する機会もあります。モードを更新する重要な動機の一つは、AES アルゴリズムのブロックサイズが、Digital Encryption Standard（DES）アルゴリズムと比べて大きい（64 ビットではなく 128 ビット）ことです。
contents.html: A mode of operation, or mode for short, is an algorithm that features the use of a symmetric key block cipher algorithm to provide an information service, such as confidentiality or authentication. With the advent of new block ciphers, such as the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), there is a need to update long-standing modes of operation and an opportunity to consider the development of new modes. One important motivation for updating modes is the increased block size of the AES algorithm compared to the Digital Encryption Standard (DES) algorithm (128 bits instead of 64 bits).

contents.html: NIST is in the process of specifying modes in the Special Publication (SP) 800-38 series. Work in 2004 focused on the second part of the series – specifying an authentication mode – and the third part – specifying a combined mode for authentication and confidentiality.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-38B『Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: The CMAC Authentication Mode』の草案は、2004 年に内部の技術レビューを受け、2005 年 3 月にパブリックコメント用に公開される見込みです。CMAC（Cipher-based Message Authentication Code）モードは、基本的に、XCBC（Extended Ciphertext Block Chaining）認証アルゴリズムの OMAC（One-key Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code）の変種です。シリーズのこの部は、2005 年に最終化される見込みです。
contents.html: A draft version of SP 800-38B, Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: The CMAC Authentication Mode, underwent internal technical review in 2004 and is expected to be released for public comment in March 2005. The CMAC (Cipher-based Message Authentication Code) mode is essentially the OMAC (One-key Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code) variation of the XCBC (Extended Ciphertext Block Chaining) authentication algorithm. This part of the series is expected to be finalized in 2005.

contents.html_ja: 行政管理予算局（OMB）は、ユーザーの遠隔識別、すなわち電子認証を、インターネットベースの政府サービスの提供における横断的な障害として特定しました。電子政府の利点を十分に実現するには、政府機関に、政府のシステムとデータの保護に合わせた電子認証のポリシーと、それに対応する技術ガイダンスが必要です。このプロジェクトは、米国政府内の電子認証のポリシー構造を確立し、連邦機関全体で電子認証の一貫した実装を促進します。この一貫性は、電子政府アプリケーションを通じてより多くの取引を行うために必要な電子的プロセスを保護することにより、政府の効率を高めるのにも役立ちます。
contents.html: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has identified the remote identification of users, or e-authentication, as a crosscutting impediment to the provision of Internet-based government services. To fully realize the benefits of electronic government, government agencies require e-authentication policies and corresponding technical guidance tailored to the protection of government systems and data. This project establishes a policy structure for e-authentication within the U.S. government, promoting consistent implementation of e-authentication across Federal agencies. This consistency will in turn help to enhance government efficiency by securing electronic processes needed to conduct more transactions through e-government applications.

contents.html_ja: OMB は 2003 年 12 月に、覚書 M-04-04『E-Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies』を発表しました。この OMB の政策覚書は、主張された身元が有効であるという保証の観点から、4 つの認証レベル（レベル 1～4）を定義しました。OMB のガイダンスは、認証の誤りによって生じる可能性の高い結果に基づいて、アプリケーションに適した認証レベルを判定するためにリスク評価を行うよう、機関に求めています。つまり、レベル 4 の認証を用いるシステム（たとえば、より機微な個人情報へのユーザーアクセスを許可するシステム）は、ユーザーの身元が本人の主張どおりであることについて、はるかに高い保証を持つということです。リスク評価を完了し、特定したリスクを必要な保証レベルに対応付けた後、OMB のガイダンスは、機関に対し、NIST の技術ガイダンスに基づいて、適切な認証機構を特定し実装するよう指示しています。
contents.html: OMB released memorandum M-04-04, E-Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies, in December 2003. This OMB policy memorandum defined four levels of authentication – Levels 1 to 4 – in terms of the assurance that an asserted identity is valid. The OMB guidance requires agencies to perform a risk assessment to determine the appropriate authentication level for an application based on the likely consequences of an authentication error. This means a system using Level 4 authentication – a system that allows a user access to more sensitive, personal information for example – has a much higher assurance that a user's identity is what it is claimed it to be. After completing a risk assessment and mapping the identified risks to the required assurance level, OMB guidance directs agencies to identify and implement appropriate authentication mechanisms based on NIST technical guidance.

contents.html_ja: 2004 年に、CSD の電子認証の技術ガイダンスが、SP 800-63『Recommendation for Electronic Authentication』として公表されました。この推奨は、電子認証を実装する機関に対し、個人が連邦の IT システムに対して自らの身元を遠隔から認証できるようにする方法についての技術ガイダンスを提供します。SP 800-63 は、身元確認と登録、トークン、遠隔認証機構、アサーション機構の各分野について、4 つの保証レベルそれぞれの具体的な技術要件を述べています。リスク評価を完了し、特定したリスクを必要な保証レベルに対応付けた後、連邦機関は SP 800-63 のガイダンスに基づいて、適切な認証機構を特定し実装できます。この刊行物は、人物と連邦の IT システムがオープンなネットワーク上で通信していることを前提としています。また、暗号鍵やパスワードなどのシークレットを所持し制御していることを個人に示させることで機能する認証機構のみを扱います。
contents.html: In 2004, CSD’s e-authentication technical guidance was published as SP 800-63, Recommendation for Electronic Authentication. This recommendation provides technical guidance to agencies implementing electronic authentication on how to allow an individual person to remote- ly authenticate his or her identity to a Federal IT system. SP 800-63 states specific technical requirements for each of the four levels of assurance in the areas of identity proofing and registration, tokens, remote authentication mechanisms and assertion mechanisms. After completing a risk assessment and mapping the identified risks to the required assurance level, Federal agencies can identify and implement appropriate authentication mechanisms based on the guidance in SP 800-63. This publication assumes the person and Federal IT system are communicating over an open network. It only addresses authentication mechanisms that work by making the individual demonstrate possession and control of a secret, such as a cryptographic key or a password.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-63 では扱っていませんが、NIST は、知識ベース認証（KBA）や遠隔生体認証など、シークレットの所持と制御に基づかない電子認証機構を研究しています。KBA の技法は、個人が持つ知識を試すことで認証を実現します。この情報はプライベートではあるものの実際にはシークレットではないため、個人の身元への確信を得ることが難しい場合があります。2004 年 2 月に NIST は、KBA のツールとソリューションに適用できる標準的な認証メトリクスを特定するため、Knowledge-Based Authentication Symposium を開催しました。生体情報は、たとえば建物への入場など、認証地点に物理的に存在する個人の認証に広く使われています。生体情報は、SP 800-63 が扱う従来の遠隔認証プロトコルで使用するのに適したシークレットではありません。ローカル認証の場合、請求者は検証者が管理する取得デバイスを使用するため、認証に生体情報を秘密にしておく必要はありません。2005 年に NIST は、遠隔認証プロトコルと生体認証を検討するワークショップを開催します。NIST は、知識ベース認証と生体認証の両方について研究を続け、ネットワーク越しに個人を遠隔認証するためのそれらの使用に関する追加のガイダンスを今後発行する可能性があります。
contents.html: While not addressed in SP 800-63, NIST is studying e-authentication mechanisms that are not based on possession and control of a secret, such as knowledge-based authentication (KBA) and remote biometrics. KBA techniques achieve authentication by testing the personal knowledge of the individual. Since this information is private but not actually secret, confidence in the identity of an individual may be hard to achieve. In February 2004, NIST hosted a Knowledge-Based Authentication Symposium to help identify standard authentication metrics that can be applied to KBA tools and solutions. Biometric methods are widely used to authenticate individuals who are physically present at the authentication point, for example, for entry into buildings. Biometrics do not constitute secrets suitable for use in the conventional remote authentication protocols addressed in SP 800-63. In the local authentication case, the claimant uses a capture device controlled by the verifier, so authentication does not require that biometrics be kept secret. In 2005, NIST will hold a workshop to examine remote authentication protocols and biometrics. NIST will continue to study both the topics of knowledge-based authentication and biometrics, and may issue additional guidance in the future on their uses for remote authentication of individuals across a network.

contents.html_ja: 個々の政府機関が電子認証技術を実装する場合、多数の機関とアプリケーションにまたがる包括的なシステムではなく、アプリケーションごとに別々の技術を実装すると、法外なコストがかかります。連邦政府は、2003 会計年度と 2004 会計年度に、整合性を欠く可能性のある、あるいは機関固有の認証・アイデンティティ管理基盤に関して、1 億 6000 万米ドルを超える額を支出しました。また、政府とやり取りする国民には、複数の資格情報を維持しなければならず、それらの資格情報を使って必要なサービスにアクセスできないという負担もあります。認証とアイデンティティ管理に機関横断のアプローチをとることが、より良い選択肢であることは明らかです。アプローチの一つであるアイデンティティ管理基盤は、認証技術と身元検証のニーズが大きく異なる環境に、拡張性とより高い費用対効果をもたらします。
contents.html: Individual government agencies implementing electronic authentication techniques would incur prohibitive costs if they were to implement separate techniques for each application instead of an umbrella system that could span numerous agencies and applications. The Federal government spent in excess of $160M in fiscal year 2003 and 2004 on potentially incon-sistent or agency-unique authentication and identity management infrastructure. There is also a burden on the public in interacting with the government by having to maintain multiple credentials and not being able to access the services they need using those credentials. It is clear that a cross-agency approach for authentication and identity management is a better alternative. One type of approach – an identity management infrastructure – brings scalability and higher cost-effectiveness to an environment of widely varying authentications techniques and identity verification needs.

contents.html: Pursuant to its responsibilities under the Electronic Government Act of 2002, OMB has determined that beginning in fiscal year 2006 Federal agencies that intend to use Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) services will be buying them from qualified managed service providers – Shared Service Providers (SSPs) – operating under the Federal Common Policy Framework rather than establishing their own internal PKI. The Common Policy Framework is a suite of uniform policies developed by NIST in 2004.
contents.html_ja: 2002 年電子政府法に基づく責任に従って、OMB は、2006 会計年度から、公開鍵基盤（PKI）サービスの利用を予定する連邦機関は、独自の内部 PKI を構築するのではなく、Federal Common Policy Framework のもとで運営される、資格を備えたマネージドサービスプロバイダ（Shared Service Provider（SSP））からそれらを購入することと決定しました。Common Policy Framework は、2004 年に NIST が策定した統一的なポリシーの集合です。

contents.html_ja: Federal Bridge Certification Authority と相互認証している PKI 運用を行う機関は、これらの新しいマネージドサービスプロバイダに移行する必要はありませんが、時間が経つにつれて、これらの新しいプロバイダへの移行が望ましくなる可能性があります。Federal Identity Credentialing Committee（FICC）は、この 2 段階のプロセスが、産業界と政府の両方のコスト削減につながると見込んでいます。第一に、各機関が独自の特異なポリシーを策定するのではなく、共通のポリシーを満たすように PKI サービスが開発されることを確保することによって、第二に、連邦機関（および General Services Administration（GSA）Schedules の他の許可されたユーザー）がタスクオーダーとデリバリーオーダーを発注できる共通の契約を持つことによってです。
contents.html: Agencies with PKI operations that are cross-certi-fied with the Federal Bridge Certification Authority will not be required to migrate to these new managed service providers, but as time goes on it may become desirable to migrate to these new providers. It is the expectation of the Federal Identity Credentialing Committee (FICC) that this two-step process will result in cost savings to both industry and government; first by insuring that PKI services are developed to meet a common policy, rather than having each agency developing its own idiosyncratic policy, and secondly by having a common contract against which task and delivery orders may be placed by Federal agencies (and other authorized users of the General Services Administration (GSA) Schedules).

contents.html: Potential SSPs must meet the requirements established in the Common Policy Framework, support smart cards that implement the Government Smart Card Interoperability Specification (GSC-IS) version 2.1 and satisfy the Federal certification and accreditation requirements. Vendors of PKI services wishing to be an SSP must meet an objective list of requirements established by the SSP Subcommittee. The SSP Subcommittee used this list of requirements to evaluate vendors’ operational procedures, review third-party audits and assess operational compliance demonstrations when establishing the initial list of three approved PKI providers.

contents.html_ja: 現在、Access Certificates for Electronic Services（ACES）プログラムや GSA のスマートカード契約のもとでサービスを利用できるのに、なぜ SSP の仕組みが必要なのかという疑問が提起されています。SSP プログラムは契約を確立するものではなく、適格な入札者の一覧を作成するものです。SSP 小委員会は、機関を 1 つのソリューションに限定したいとは考えていません。SSP 小委員会が望んでいるのは、機関が PKI サービスを契約する際に最低限のセキュリティと品質の水準を確保する、連邦政府での共通のポリシーを実装した PKI の標準を設定することです。
contents.html: It has been asked why the SSP system is necessary when services are currently available under the Access Certificates for Electronic Services (ACES) program or the GSA smart card contract. The SSP Program does not establish a contract but creates a qualified bidders list. The SSP Subcommittee does not want to limit agencies to one solution. The SSP Subcommittee does want to set a standard for PKI that implements a common policy in the Federal government that ensures a minimum level of security and quality when agencies contract for PKI services.

The Shared Service Provider Roadmap is intended to identify the background information, phases and activities related to the selection process for prospective PKI managed service providers. This document identifies the process by which a vendor qualifies for inclusion on the Qualified Bidders List. The document also describes requirements that must be met to maintain qual-ification, as well as contracting considerations.

contents.html_ja: また、GSA によるオンライン電子認証資格情報検証インフラの開発も支援しています。GSA の e-Authentication Gateway は、政府のアプリケーションと非政府の CSP の間を仲介し、アプリケーションがさまざまな識別用資格情報を受け入れられるようにします。たとえば、個人は、銀行で確立したパスワードなどの認証機構を、政府のアプリケーションへのアクセスに活用する場合があります。GSA の E-Authentication Gateway のアーキテクチャは、CSP や政府のアプリケーションと認証情報を交換するために、SAML、TLS、PKI に依存しています。NIST は、E-Authentication Gateway、CSP、政府のアプリケーションの間での、TLS で保護された認証情報の送信を支える PKI のアーキテクチャと PKI のポリシーを開発することにより、GSA を支援しました。
contents.html: We are also assisting GSA in the development of an online e-authentication credential validation infrastructure. The GSA e-Authentication Gateway will mediate between government applications and non-government CSPs, permit-ting applications to accept a variety of identification credentials. For example, individuals may be able to leverage authentication mechanisms, such as passwords, established with their banks to access government applications. The GSA E-Authentication Gateway architecture relies on SAML, TLS and PKI to exchange authentication information with CSPs and government applications. NIST assisted GSA by developing PKI architecture and PKI policies supporting TLS- protected transmission of authentication information between the E-Authentication Gateway, CSPs and government applications.

contents.html_ja: このプロジェクトの一環として、NIST は、Simple Object Access Protocol（SOAP）や Security Assertion Markup Language（SAML）を含む Web サービスのプロトコル、パスワードの効果的な使用、登録と身元確認を研究しています。Federal PKI Policy Authority（FPKIPA）、FICC、GSA、政府説明責任局（GAO）、国家安全保障局（NSA）、連邦預金保険公社（FDIC）、OMB、イリノイ州とワシントン州、そして 1,800 の大学、カレッジ、教育機関を含む EduCause など、多くの主体と連携しています。
contents.html: As part of this project, NIST is researching Web services protocols including Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) and Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), effective password use and registration and identity proofing. We are collaborating with many entities, including the Federal PKI Policy Authority (FPKIPA), FICC, GSA, the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the National Security Agency (NSA), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), OMB, the States of Illinois and Washington and EduCause, which includes 1,800 universities, colleges and educational institutions.

contents.html_ja: Software Diagnostics and Conformance Testing Division の NIST スマートカードチームは、John Wack、Teresa Schwarzhoff、James Dray、Alan Goldfine（左から右）で構成され、スマートカードアプリケーション間の相互運用性を飛躍的に高め、米国政府の要件を集約し、スマートカードに関する世界有数の専門家との連携を築いた枠組みと仕様の策定により、2004 年ゴールドメダル賞を受賞しました。NIST スマートカードチームの業績は、政府機関のセキュリティを飛躍的に高めると同時に、市場全体を米国企業に開くことに貢献しました。
contents.html: The NIST Smart Card Team, consisting of (left to right) John Wack, Teresa Schwarzhoff, James Dray, and Alan Goldfine, Software Diagnostics and Conformance Testing Division, received the 2004 Gold Medal Award for the development of a framework and specification that dramatically advanced interoperability among smart card applications, coalesced U.S. government requirements and forged alliances with the world’s foremost authorities on smart cards. The work of the NIST Smart Card Team served to open an entire market to U.S. businesses while dramatically increasing the security of government agencies.

contents.html_ja: Alicia Clay と Michael Hogan（ITL）は、論文「Securely Connecting the World with Cyber Security Standards」により、世界標準の日 2004 論文コンペティションで第 1 位を受賞しました。1990 年以来、米国の標準化コミュニティは、国際標準化機構（ISO）、国際電気標準会議（IEC）、国際電気通信連合（ITU）が定めた世界標準の日を毎年祝っています。2004 年の祝賀のテーマは「Standards Connect the World」でした。NIST と ANSI が共同議長を務め、約 50 の業界団体、専門学会、標準策定団体、企業、政府機関が参加した米国の祝賀行事は、国の経済と消費者にとっての標準化の価値に敬意を表しました。この論文は、Standards Engineering: The Journal of the Standards Engineering Society の 2004 年 11/12 月号に掲載されました。
contents.html: Alicia Clay and Michael Hogan (ITL) were awarded First Place in the World Standards Day 2004 Paper Competition for their paper, “Securely Connecting the World with Cyber Security Standards.” Since 1990, the U.S. standards community has annually observed World Standards Day, so designated by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Telecommunications Union (ITU). The theme for the 2004 celebration was “Standards Connect the World.” The U.S.celebration,co-chaired by NIST and ANSI with participation by some 50 trade associations, professional societies, standards development organizations, corporations and government agencies, paid tribute to the value of standardization to the Nation's economy and the consuming public. The paper was published in the November/December 2004 issue of Standards Engineering: The Journal of the Standards Engineering Society.

contents.html_ja: Joan Hash は、Federal Computer Week により、2004 年の「Fed 100」賞の受賞者に選ばれました。この賞の審査員は、機関またはコミュニティ全体に目に見える貢献をした人物を探します。Ms. Hash は、セキュリティマネジメントのガイドラインの策定に主要な指針を与え、全体の品質と、法律、ポリシー、その他の既存のセキュリティガイドラインとの一貫性を確保するため、主要なレビュアーを務め、多くの場合は共著者も務めたことにより、表彰されました。
contents.html: Joan Hash was selected by Federal Computer Week to receive a 2004 “Fed 100” Award. The judges for these awards look for someone who has made a noticeable difference in an agency or in the community at large. Ms. Hash was recognized for providing principal direction to the development of security management guidelines and serving as key reviewer and often co-author to ensure overall quality and consistency with legal, policy and other existing security guidelines.

contents.html_ja: Tanya Brewer は、Presidential Management Fellows Program を修了し、その修了生となりました。Presidential Management Fellows Program は、公共政策とプログラムの分析・管理におけるリーダーシップに対する並外れた能力と、明確な関心と意欲を示す、幅広い学問分野の優秀な大学院生を連邦政府の職務に引きつけるため、1977 年に大統領令によって創設されました。フェローシップは毎年 400 人以下に授与されます。Ms. Brewer は、CSD の職員であることに加えて、第 108 議会の期間中に、Ron Wyden 米国上院議員の事務所での一時派遣を修了しました。
contents.html: Tanya Brewer completed and became an alumnus of the Presidential Management Fellows Program. The Presidential Management Fellows Program was established by Executive Order in 1977 to attract to the Federal service outstanding graduate students from a wide variety of academic disciplines who demonstrate an exceptional ability for, as well as a clear interest in and commitment to, leadership in the analysis and management of public policies and programs. Not more than 400 Fellowships are awarded annually. In addition to being a CSD staff member, Ms. Brewer completed a temporary detail in the Office of U.S. Senator Ron Wyden during the 108th Congress.

contents.html: Opportunities are available at NIST for 6 to 24-month internships within the CSD. Qualified individuals should contact the CSD, provide a statement of qualifications and indicate the area of work that is of interest. Generally speaking, the salary costs are borne by the sponsoring institution; however, in some cases, these guest research internships carry a small monthly stipend paid by NIST. For further information, contact Mr. Ed Roback, (301) 975-2934, edward.roback@nist.gov.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、さまざまな方法で産業界と学界の研究に資金を提供しています。Advanced Technology Program は、産業界と共同で、リスクが高く見返りの大きいプロジェクトに資金を提供します。Small Business Innovation Research Program は、中小企業からの研究開発の提案に資金を提供します。また、精密測定、火災研究、材料科学といった特定分野の取り組みを奨励するため、その他の助成金も提供しています。産業界、学界、その他の機関での研究を支援する助成金／賞は、NIST の複数の部署を通じて、競争方式で提供されています。NIST の助成金プログラムの一般的な情報は、Ms. Joyce Brigham（(301) 975-6329、joyce.brigham@nist.gov）にお問い合わせください。
contents.html: NIST funds industrial and academic research in a variety of ways. Our Advanced Technology Program co-funds high-risk, high-payoff projects with industry. The Small Business Innovation Research Program funds R&D proposals from small businesses. We also offer other grants to encourage work in specific fields: precision measurement, fire research and materials science. Grants/awards supporting research at industry, academic and other institutions are available on a competitive basis through several different Institute offices. For general information on NIST grants programs, contact Ms. Joyce Brigham, (301) 975-6329, joyce.brigham@nist.gov.

And, no kidding, get paid while you're learning. original_blocks.html: Among the highlights of our work in 2004 was a challenge from the President, issued in Homeland Security Presidential Directive #12, to develop a new standard for identification and verification of Federal employees and contractors. We continued making progress in fulfilling the mandates of the Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 which resulted in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems, and NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems. In addressing the President’s challenge, we drew heavily upon our ongoing smart card, biometric and cryptographic work. As such, we made great strides towards a framework for protecting Federal facilities, systems and the employees who have access to them. The long-term benefit of using FIPS 199, SP 800-53 and a standards-based approach to system security in general is more targeted, cost-effective, consistent and improved security.

original_blocks.html: While the interconnection of information systems often increases the risk to an organization’s operations and assets, FIPS 199 and our associated suite of standards and guidelines provide a common way to express information security requirements. This in turn promotes greater consistency across diverse organizations in managing risks.

original_blocks.html: Scientists in the Computer Security Division have been working with our partners for the past several years to establish a Government Smart Card (GSC) program to facilitate widespread deployment of interoperable smart card systems. In recognition of this work, the NIST Smart Card Team received the Department of Commerce’s 2004 Gold Medal Award for the development of a framework and specification that dramatically advanced interoperability among smart card applications, coalesced U.S. government requirements and forged alliances with the world’s foremost authorities on smart cards.

original_blocks.html: The Division has had many other accomplishments this past year, including advancing development of our cryptographic standards toolkit, further e-authentication work, expansion of our Cryptographic Module Validation Program, development of an IT product security configuration checklist program and more work with digital forensics tools and methods. We have begun new work, as well as continuing previous work, on several key Internet security protocols – IPSec, BGP and DNSSEC. We have also provided technical expertise to several U.S. government groups on the security implications of spam e-mail and phishing attacks.

original_blocks.html: These are just some of the highlights of our work this year. We invite you to read more about our work – and to work with us – as we address these and future challenges. Our extraordinarily talented and knowledgeable experts are recognized as leaders in their fields. Many have come to us from the private sector and other agencies, bringing with them a diverse set of perspectives and expertise and a solid commitment to public service. We are proud to highlight their achievements in this report and to note the honors and awards that were received this year celebrating their achievements.

original_blocks.html: The Federal Information Systems Security Educators Association (FISSEA) is an organization run by and for Federal information systems security professionals. FISSEA assists Federal agencies in meeting their computer security training responsibilities. FISSEA strives to elevate the general level of information systems security knowledge for the Federal government and the federally-related workforce. FISSEA serves as a professional forum for the exchange of information and improvement of information systems security awareness, training and education programs. It also seeks to provide for the professional development of its members.

original_blocks.html: Membership is open to information systems security professionals, trainers, educators and managers who are responsible for information systems security training programs in Federal agencies, as well as contractors of these agencies and faculty members of accredited educational institutions. There are no membership fees for FISSEA; all that is required is a willingness to share products, information and experiences. Business is administered by a twelve-member Executive Board that meets monthly. Board members serve two- year terms and elections are held during the annual conference. Each year an award is presented to a candidate selected as Educator of the Year honoring distinguished accomplishments in information systems security training programs. There is also a contest for computer security posters, Web sites and awareness tools with the winning entries listed on the FISSEA Web site. FISSEA has a quarterly newsletter, an actively maintained Web site and a listserve as a means of communication for members. Members are encouraged to participate in the annual FISSEA conference and to serve on the FISSEA ad-hoc task groups. CSD assists FISSEA with its operations by providing staff support for several of its activities and by being FISSEA’s host agency.

Demonstrations,” in May 2004.The workshop was presented by the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Training Center for Information Assurance training team. Attendees were invited to participate in this interactive workshop on the process of designing information assurance training programs to meet Federal guidelines. The workshop began with an overview of the NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-16, Information Technology Security Training Requirements: A Role- and Performance-Based Model. Next, discussion provided attendees with an overview of three primary information assurance (IA) training categories: Management Controls, Operational Controls and Technical Controls. Based on these categories, attendees generated a list of topics, learning objectives, presentation modes, learning activities and learning measurement strategies for three specific IA roles – Managers, System Administrators and Information System Security Officers (ISSOs). This gave the attendees realistic training that would transfer to their agency’s awareness and training program.

Low / Moderate / High
Confidentiality Preserving authorized restrictions on information access and disclosure, including means for protecting personal privacy and proprietary information. Integrity Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity. [44 U.S.C., SEC. 3542]The unauthorized modification or destruction of information could be expected to have a limitedadverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals. / The unauthorized modification or destruction of information could be expected to have a seriousadverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals. / The unauthorized modification or destruction of information could be expected to have a severe or catastrophicadverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.
Availability Ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information. [44 U.S.C., SEC. 3542]The disruption of access to or use of information or an information system could be expected to have a limited adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals. / The disruption of access to or use of information or an information system could be expected to have a serious adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals. / The disruption of access to or use of information or an information system could be expected to have a severe or catastrophicadverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

original_blocks.html: Alicia Clay and Michael Hogan (ITL) were awarded First Place in the World Standards Day 2004 Paper Competition for their paper, “Securely Connecting the World with Cyber Security Standards.” Since 1990, the U.S. standards community has annually observed World Standards Day, so designated by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Telecommunications Union (ITU). The theme for the 2004 celebration was “Standards Connect the World.” The U.S.celebration,co-chaired by NIST and ANSI with participation by some 50 trade associations, professional societies, standards development organizations, corporations and government agencies, paid tribute to the value of standardization to the Nation's economy and the consuming public. The paper was published in the November/December 2004 issue of Standards Engineering: The Journal of the Standards Engineering Society.

original_blocks.html: This guide includes security templates that will enable system administrators to apply the security recommendations rapidly. The NIST Windows XP Security Templates are text-based configuration files that specify values for security-relevant system settings. The security templates modify several key policy areas of a Windows XP system, including password policy, account lockout policy, auditing policy, user rights assignment, system security options, event log policy, system service settings and file permissions. The templates are based on security templates previously developed by the National Security Agency (NSA), Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) and Microsoft. Most of the settings in the templates represent consensus recommendations as proposed by various security experts from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Center for Internet Security (CIS), DISA, NSA, Microsoft and NIST.

original_blocks.html: Homeland Security Presidential Directive #12 (HSPD-12) mandated the Secretary of Commerce to develop a Federal standard for government-wide secure and reliable forms of identification and a smart card is the chosen technology. The Federal government has embraced smart card technology because of the inherent security features and versatility of this technology. For example, a single smart card could be used as an identification card, to provide access to secure buildings, to securely logon to computer systems and to make small purchases. Approximately 30 to 40 million smart cards are due to be issued within the next few years for government purposes.

original_blocks.html: Ad hoc networks are well suited for sensor networks comprised of small wireless electronic devices that can measure and monitor events and physical properties such as tempera-ture, movement, pressure and location. These sensors can be used to provide visual and audio feedback in environments not easily accessible by humans. Inexpensive wireless sensors can be used to monitor bridges, factories, highways and buildings, for example, to help improve public safety. Mobile handheld devices such as personal digital assistants (PDAs) and laptops can be used by first responders and by today's emerging mobile workforce to easily and quickly set up networks to communicate with their peers. The goal of this research is to develop and test security mechanisms that support secure routing, communication and intrusion detection within small-scale wireless mobile ad-hoc networks (MANET).

original_blocks.html: Quality of Service (QoS) is fundamental to the operation of a VoIP network that meets users’ quality expectations. However, the implementation of various security measures can cause a marked deterioration in QoS unless VoIP-specific equipment and architectures are used. These complications range from firewalls delaying or blocking call setups to encryption-produced latency and delay variation (jitter). Because of the time-critical nature of VoIP and its low tolerance for disruption and packet loss, many security measures implemented in traditional data networks are simply not applicable to VoIP in their current form; firewalls, intrusion detection systems and other components must be specialized for VoIP. Most current VoIP systems use one of two standards – H.323 or the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). Although SIP seems to be gaining in popularity, neither of these protocols has become dominant in the market yet, so it often makes sense to incorporate components that can support both.

original_blocks.html: Quantum mechanics, the strange behavior of matter on the atomic scale, provides entirely new and uniquely powerful tools for computing and communications. This field could revolu-tionize many aspects of computing and secure communications, and could have enormous impacts on homeland security. Whereas current computers calculate linearly, quantum computers will be able to calculate enormous number of variables simultaneously. This capability is particularly useful in modeling complex situations with many variables (weather modeling, for example) and in solving extremely difficult equations (processing tasks that would literally take billions of years on conventional computers).

original_blocks.html: During the past year, we have begun work on Special Publication (SP) 800-77, Guide to IPSec VPNs. This document will describe the three primary models for VPN architectures – gateway-to-gateway, host-to-gateway and host-to-host. These models can be used, respectively, to connect two secured networks (such as a branch office and headquarters) over the Internet, to protect communications for hosts on unsecured networks (such as traveling employees), or to secure direct communications between two computers that require extra protection.
